neighbours.label: Leading indentation or an opening quote at the start of a line inside indented Python (docstring parameter lines, dictionary keys, '_new_' helper names)
quiet: The function takes a shape callable and a validation flag, and it returns a tensor of the same shape as its input.
The table lists total precipitation in inches, growing degree days and the average temperature for each month.
A helper creates a new event object, and it is used when the worker threads need to wait for a signal.
The configuration object holds a name and a size, and both are read from a file when the program starts.
Labels are shown in English by default, and the user can switch to metric units in the settings dialog.
A lock is created for each thread, and it is released when the work item has been put on the queue.
The docs say the call returns a tensor, and that an error is raised if the input shapes differ.
Colour names are mapped to hex codes, and the theme picks one of them for the page background.

notes: Heterogeneous top examples (indentation runs, a quote, '_new', an email dot, base64); expected to fail.
